query: I'm building a natural history model of bladder cancer and need to fit the progression rates to SEER age-specific incidence plus the stage distribution at diagnosis. I have cases and person-years for 18 age bands. Where do I even start with setting this up in R?
my IMIS run finishes but the ESS column ends up around 40 out of 1000 and maxweight stays at like 0.3. 11 parameters. is that salvageable or do i need a different algorithm

Calibrated a 3-state model to survival data. Posterior mean is 0.088/0.084, the credible intervals cover basically the entire prior, and the two params correlate at -0.97. But the best-fitting set matches the targets almost perfectly. I don't understand what the posterior is telling me.
Before I burn three days of cluster time — is there a way to check whether my prior ranges can even produce my calibration targets, and whether 5 parameters is too many for the 2 targets I've got?

We have an existing calibration in R-labs that fits to survival only. Reviewer wants us to also match disease prevalence over time. What do I need to change in the likelihood and does adding it change how I should weight things?

my incidence targets are counts per age group and the model gives me a rate. right now im using dnorm on the rates with SEs i calculated but the fit is completely dominated by the 75+ age groups and the residuals look way overdispersed. what likelihood should i actually be using

Three of the transition probabilities in my cSTM can't be measured directly — there's no study that reports them. I do have registry data on prevalence and mortality. How do I go about estimating the three from that?

Each evaluation of my microsimulation takes about 4 seconds and the calibration needs maybe 50k evaluations. Should I be parallelising the likelihood across the parameter sets, and if so how do I set that up so it works on both my mac and the linux cluster?

ran optim with Nelder-Mead from 100 random starting points on my sick-sicker model. they all converge to the same log-likelihood value but two totally different parameter vectors depending on where they start. is my optimiser broken?

I'm writing the calibration lab for my decision-modeling course next quarter. Want to walk them through random search then Nelder-Mead then a Bayesian method on the same toy model, and show why the Bayesian one is worth the extra effort. Can you draft the scripts?

I fit a logistic regression to predict 30-day readmission and the reviewers want calibration assessed. Can you help me produce a calibration plot with the calibration slope and intercept, plus the Brier score and a Hosmer-Lemeshow test?

Here's my calibration script from a project two years ago — R/calibrate_imis.R, about 400 lines. It works but takes 6 hours. Can you look through it and tell me if there are bugs and where the time is going?

My model is already calibrated and I've got 1000 posterior parameter sets saved. Now I need to run the PSA, produce a CEAC and compute the expected value of perfect information across a range of willingness-to-pay thresholds.

Need to write the Methods paragraph describing our calibration approach for the MDM submission. We used IMIS with uniform priors over 6 parameters and 4 target series. Draft about 250 words with the right level of technical detail for that journal?
Reviewer 2 says our calibration targets were 'selected post hoc to favour the intervention arm' which is not true, we prespecified them. How should I phrase the response without sounding defensive?

I've got individual-level cohort data in a data.table, about 40k rows, and want to fit a Weibull survival model with age and stage as covariates, then use the fitted parameters somewhere else. Which package and what's the syntax?
why does my markov trace stop summing to 1 around cycle 40? the row sums drift to like 0.9997 and then it gets worse. transition matrix is built in Functions_markov.R

Two strategies, costs and QALYs from my model. I need incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, the efficiency frontier with dominated strategies removed, and a net monetary benefit table at 50k and 100k per QALY.

our lab spectrophotometer drifts and needs recalibrating against the standard curve every few weeks. is there an R workflow for fitting the standard curve and flagging when readings go out of tolerance?
Can you explain what a hazard ratio actually means to a policy audience with no stats background? Writing a one-paragraph plain-language summary for a policy brief.
